author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Untrusted page parameter is clamped at the boundary (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)) before any use, and the clamped value threads to both the repository query and the view model - no unclamped path remains in processFindForm

Integer overflow on page - 1 is closed: the prior page=-2147483648 path overflowed to Integer.MAX_VALUE and produced a huge offset query; the clamp makes page >= 1 so page - 1 cannot wrap, and Spring's PageRequest computes offset as a long

Information disclosure via the error page is reduced, not widened: the unhandled IllegalArgumentException from PageRequest.of no longer reaches the error view, which renders the underlying exception message (docs/security-principles.md, secret-disclosure row). No new exception message carrying internal detail is introduced
No injection surface added: pagination still flows through the Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith with a bound Pageable; no string-concatenated query text

No XSS surface added: currentPage reaches owners/ownersList.html only as a primitive int used in numeric comparisons and Thymeleaf link preprocessing, so no attacker-controlled text enters markup and default escaping is untouched
Unbounded upper page values remain a bounded-cost empty-result path (query returns empty, controller renders the not-found form); no new exposure beyond the documented baseline
No new endpoint, no binder change, no widening of management exposure; the @InitBinder identifier disallow list is untouched
Supply chain unchanged: the change set touches only OwnerController.java and PetClinicIntegrationTests.java - no build.gradle edit, no new dependency, no repository or TLS-check change
No hardcoded credentials, tokens, keys, or other secrets in either changed file; the added integration test uses only the ephemeral local test port

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The new FIRST_PAGE constant (=1) is the single source of truth for the page floor, but the @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") annotation on the same method still hardcodes the literal "1" instead of referencing it. If FIRST_PAGE is ever changed, the annotation default silently drifts out of sync with the clamp floor, and nothing would catch it at compile time.
findings.fix: Change `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1")` to `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "" + FIRST_PAGE)` (a valid compile-time constant expression) so the two stay linked to one declaration.

approved_aspects: Fix is minimal and correctly scoped to the reported bug: clamps at the boundary with Math.max instead of adding broad input validation machinery
Clamped currentPage value is threaded consistently to both the repository query and addPaginationModel, avoiding a mismatch between the page requested and the page rendered
New FIRST_PAGE constant is a clear, well-named replacement for a bare magic number in the clamp expression
Test covers both boundary values (0 and -1) via a small parameterized loop rather than duplicated test methods, and formatting passes ./gradlew checkFormat

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Assertion strength is too weak to pin the claimed behavior: the test only checks HTTP 200 for page=0 and page=-1. Before the fix, PageRequest.of(page-1,5) throws for page<=0 and the framework's default error handler still can return 200 with an HTML error body in some configurations, and after a hypothetical wrong fix (e.g. clamping to a page number beyond the last page) findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would return an empty Page, triggering the 'no owners found' branch (view owners/findOwners, still HTTP 200). Confirmed against the seed data (10 owners in db/h2/data.sql, page size 5 -> 2 pages): a response that silently lands on the wrong view still passes this test. Strengthen the assertion to verify the actual first-page content or view, e.g. assert the response body contains a first-page owner (e.g. 'Franklin') and/or compare it against an explicit page=1 request, not status code alone.
findings.fix: Add a body/content assertion (or compare against an explicit ?page=1 request) so the test fails if page=0 lands on the wrong view or wrong page slice, not just on a 5xx.

findings.description: Test body contains a `for` loop over page values ("0", "-1") with the assertion inside the loop. testing-principles.md Test Structure requires straight-line test bodies with no loops; the Agent Decision Checklist item 4 (Linearity) applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward, which this new test is. The pre-existing loop pattern elsewhere in this same file (processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace) is legacy debt, not a precedent to extend into new tests.
findings.fix: Convert to a @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(ints = {0, -1}) (or @CsvSource) so each page value is an independent, named test case instead of a manual loop.

findings.description: Method name `ownerListTreatsPageBelowOneAsFirstPage` mirrors the surrounding file's pre-2026-07-31 naming (method-name-as-description), not the brief's BDD naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`) that applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward.
findings.fix: Rename to something like `theOwnerListShouldTreatPageBelowOneAsFirstPage` to match the mandated naming school for newly-written tests.

approved_aspects: Test placement in PetClinicIntegrationTests (real repository, real HTTP, no mocks) correctly follows the Mocking Policy's 'real I/O for integration' rule and avoids extending the pre-existing @MockitoBean pattern in OwnerControllerTests for a new test — a sound call given the brief tolerates but discourages growing mock-framework usage

Confirmed the fix is load-bearing: without the Math.max clamp, PageRequest.of(page-1,5) with page<=0 throws IllegalArgumentException (negative page index), which the seeded 10-owner/page-size-5 dataset actually triggers via findPaginatedForOwnersLastName — the added test does exercise a real defect and would fail without the fix
Full suite (./gradlew test) passes with the new test included; no regressions

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test only asserts HttpStatus.OK for page=0 and page=-1. That proves the request no longer throws, but does not prove the stated fix behavior - 'treats any page value below 1 as the first page.' A regression that clamped to a different page, or any page value that happens not to throw, would still pass this test. The ownersList view renders currentPage from the model (used to disable the 'first'/'previous' pagination controls when currentPage<=1), so the response body for page=0 and page=-1 should be asserted equal to the body of an explicit page=1 request for the same query, or at minimum should assert the first-page-disabled markup is present and no link back to page=0/page=-1 exists. As written this is only a crash-regression test, not a test of the boundary semantics the fix claims to deliver.
findings.fix: Add a body-content assertion for both page=0 and page=-1: compare the response body to the body of an explicit /owners?lastName=&page=1 request (same query), or assert the rendered page shows the first-page-disabled pagination markers.

recommendations: The new clamp (Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)) in OwnerController.processFindForm is pure logic with no I/O dependency, yet its only test coverage boots the full Spring context, a real embedded servlet container, and a real HTTP client (PetClinicIntegrationTests is the heaviest tier in this suite). testing-principles.md's Test Pyramid section asks of each new controller rule: could this have been tested without booting the framework? The implementer's stated reason for avoiding OwnerControllerTests (its existing @MockitoBean repository mock) is a legitimate application of the mocking policy, but placing the test at the heaviest tier instead of extracting the page-resolution step into a small framework-free helper (unit-testable) widens the pyramid gap the brief already flags as a known debt. Worth a decision, not necessarily a blocking one: if the team judges this one-line rule too trivial/coupled to extract, that is defensible, but it should be a conscious call rather than a placement default.
approved_aspects: Test genuinely fails without the fix: with no clamp, page=0/-1 flow into PageRequest.of(page-1, ...) with a negative index, which throws IllegalArgumentException; OwnerController has no @ExceptionHandler and there is no global @ControllerAdvice in the app, so the exception reaches Spring Boot's default error handling and returns a non-200 status - the added test is not vacuous against the pre-fix code.

Choosing PetClinicIntegrationTests over extending the @MockitoBean-based OwnerControllerTests is consistent with the brief's mocking policy, which tolerates but does not encourage new tests reaching for an existing mock-framework stub.
Test structure follows four-phase shape with real I/O (real embedded DB via the Spring context) and no invented/mocked collaborators beyond the sanctioned in-process web harness.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owners page param at the first page

blast_radius.note: Three files, two modules, eight hunks, no sensitive paths; the production edit is confined to OwnerController.processFindForm, and the only other file touched is CLAUDE.md's stale Gradle task names, which I verified against build.gradle (the io.spring.javaformat plugin does supply format/checkFormat, and no stale formatJava/checkJavaFormat reference survives anywhere in the tree).

semantic_surprise.note: I read every hunk: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) clamps at the low boundary only, both downstream call sites (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) receive the clamped currentPage so the rendered pagination widget cannot emit a page=0 or negative link, the raw page param is used nowhere else in the method, and the concatenated defaultValue is a compile-time constant expression that still resolves to the string 1, leaving default and above-range behaviour unchanged.

test_adequacy.note: The added parameterized test over the values 0 and -1 drives real HTTP against the real repository and asserts both HTTP 200 and body equality with an explicit page=1 request, so it fails against the pre-fix code (which threw and rendered the error page) and would also catch a clamp that reached the repository but not the view model; body equality subsumes the currentPage and totalPages attributes rather than restating the implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: Every reviewer the plan dispatched (code-quality, test, doc) approved, security approved in round one with zero findings, and the four round-one findings were all autofix-tagged with zero escalations and no bar_clause rework, so nothing in the roster reads as approval-with-reservations.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries; the diff stays on the /owners page-param surface the requirement names, and the CLAUDE.md hunk is a bounded three-line doc correction raised as a doc-reviewer finding inside the slice rather than an unrelated ride-along.

rationale: Read all eight hunks: the clamp is one-sided at the correct boundary and threads to both the query and the view model, so no pagination link can regress. Confirm and merge. Separately, VetController.findPaginated carries the identical unclamped page-minus-one and wants its own slice.
